title: "4. Listen Like an Engineer"
description: "Review the produced audio, evaluate it against the five-dimension rubric, and iterate. Produce evaluation.md."
order: 8

## Overview

Producing an audio file is **not** completion. Generation produces a draft;
engineering judgment decides whether it teaches the right thing, clearly, in a
way a listener can follow and later explain. This lesson teaches you to review
your audio as an engineer: check the technical truth, then evaluate, record
findings, and iterate.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

- Explain why generation is not completion.
- Review audio for technical correctness, educational effectiveness, narrative
  clarity, and audio quality.
- Apply the five-dimension evaluation rubric, with technical accuracy weighted
  significantly.
- Trace a defect back to its origin stage and fix it there.
- Record findings and iterate to a passing artifact.

## Generation is not completion

The renderer turns your screenplay into sound. But a beautiful production that
teaches the *wrong* architecture must not pass just because it is entertaining.
The produced audio is a draft that needs engineering review.

Review the audio on four fronts:

- **Technical correctness** — does the metaphor still accurately describe the
  system? Have any facts drifted as you wrote dialogue and narration?
- **Educational effectiveness** — could someone unfamiliar with the technology
  explain the important concepts afterward?
- **Narrative clarity** — can the listener tell who is speaking, where the scene
  occurs, what happened, and why it matters?
- **Audio quality** — voice distinction, pronunciation, pacing, silence,
  ambience, sound levels, effects, and scene transitions.

## The five-dimension rubric

Score your artifact across five dimensions, each answering one question:

| Dimension | Question |
| --- | --- |
| Technical accuracy | Does the story correctly represent the engineering concept? |
| Metaphor quality | Does the metaphor improve understanding without introducing serious misconceptions? |
| Narrative clarity | Can the listener follow the story without visual assistance? |
| Audio communication | Do voice, narration, and sound communicate actions and context effectively? |
| Learning outcome | Can the listener explain the underlying technical model afterward? |

### Weighting

Technical accuracy carries **significant weight**. A passing artifact must teach
the right architecture. A typical weighting: technical accuracy at 40%, with the
other dimensions sharing the remainder.

::: {.callout-tip}
Play the audio to someone unfamiliar with the technology and ask them to explain
the concept back. This is the strongest test of learning outcome and educational
effectiveness — and it will expose technical drift you may have gone blind to.
:::

## Tracing defects to their origin

Each stage of your pipeline is inspectable, so defects trace to a stage:

| Symptom | Likely origin | Fix where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wrong architecture conveyed | The model was wrong or misunderstood | `concept.md` / the real docs |
| Misleading comparison | The metaphor mis-fits the model | `metaphor.md` |
| Confusing dialogue | The story didn't carry the relationship | `scenes.md` / `screenplay.md` |
| Wrong pronunciation / bad pacing | The renderer | `production.md` |

When you find a defect, fix it at its origin — do not try to patch audio with a
voice-over. If the metaphor is wrong, fix the metaphor, not the recording.

## Recording findings and iterating

Record your findings in an `evaluation.md` file:

```yaml
dimensions:
  technical_accuracy: { score: 4, notes: "..." }
  metaphor_quality:   { score: 4, notes: "..." }
  narrative_clarity:  { score: 5, notes: "..." }
  audio_communication:{ score: 4, notes: "..." }
  learning_outcome:   { score: 4, notes: "..." }

weighted_total: 4.2
verdict: pass   # or: needs-revision

findings:
  - "The service-bell SFX is too quiet under the kitchen ambience."
  - verification_notes: "..."
```

Then iterate: fix the highest-impact defect first, re-render, and re-evaluate.
A pass requires technical accuracy to hold — a wrong architecture cannot pass,
however enjoyable it is.
